notes: Second autonomous sprint on PR #14, run after an independent second-opinion audit of the P0 sprint. Values copied from persisted run artifacts. Validation only; test was never loaded or scored during this sprint.

experiments.hypothesis: Replacing standard pointwise BCE training with a vectorized joint Pointwise-BCE + Within-User Listwise Softmax loss (L = L_BCE + lambda * L_Listwise) using GradientFM and user_groups will directly optimize relative item ordering within each user group during SGD, raising validation GAUC and nDCG@5 beyond 0.60232 while executing in <150 seconds.

Filtering the training data to retain only train users with within-user target variance (at least 2 impressions with both positive and negative labels) will focus SGD gradient updates entirely on informative relative preference pairs, leading to sharper within-user feature representations and raising validation primary beyond 0.60232.

Combining Parent A's within-user variance row identification (retaining 100% of informative preference pair rows) with Parent B's full dataset coverage via dynamic per-epoch stochastic subsampling (15%) of uninformative user rows will maintain sharp relative preference updates while preserving global item frequency and base-rate calibration, raising validation primary beyond 0.60239.

Combining 4 FM ensemble members trained on Parent A's target-variance filtered rows with 4 FM ensemble members trained on Parent B's full dataset creates a heterogeneous data subagging ensemble. Averaging raw predictions from both distributions will fuse sharp relative preference scoring with global catalog representation, pushing validation primary beyond 0.60239.

Combining Parent A's heterogeneous multi-dataset ensembling framework with Parent B's target-variance data selection—extended into a 3-tier filtering architecture (Strict-Variance with tot>=3, Moderate-Variance with tot>=2, and Full Catalog) coupled with tier-adaptive L2 regularization (1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6)—will create a multi-granularity ensemble that captures high-confidence within-user preference pairs while preserving broad catalog feature representations and preventing subagging overfitting, raising validation primary beyond 0.60246.

Fusing Parent A's 3-tier variance filtering setup (Strict tot>=3, Moderate tot>=2, Full) and tier-adaptive L2 regularization (1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6) with Parent B's 50% full-catalog ensemble allocation (2 Strict + 2 Moderate + 4 Full catalog SWA FM members, total 8 models) will maintain Parent A's high GAUC while recovering Parent B's superior top-k nDCG@5, raising validation primary beyond 0.60252.

Fusing Parent A's catalog-balanced 2/2/4 tier allocation with Parent B's multi-granularity tier parameterization—extended to tier-adaptive latent embedding dimension k (k=8 for Strict tot>=3, k=16 for Moderate tot>=2, k=32 for Full catalog)—will allow Full catalog models to capture rich higher-order sparse feature interactions while preventing overfitting on variance-filtered subsets, pushing validation primary beyond 0.60290.

best_candidate.mechanism: 8-member FM ensemble with top-2 checkpoint SWA per member, probability mean. Members split across three tiers differing in train-row selection AND L2: 2x strict (users with >=3 impressions and mixed labels, l2=1e-4), 2x moderate (>=2 impressions and mixed labels, l2=1e-5), 4x full train split (l2=1e-6).
best_candidate.discovered_by: autonomous crossover of 007 x 006; no human supplied any tier, L2 or allocation value
best_candidate.mechanism_execution_evidence: stdout shows 8 distinct members training with three different l2 values and two filtered row counts (1129780 and 1130240 of 1141112), each early-stopping at a different epoch.

reproduction.type_b_note: All three seeds beat the frozen SWA7 elite (0.6023186); the worst is +0.000585. Seed 42 is kept because it is the agent's own choice. Selecting seed 2024 after seeing the sweep would be selection across replicates.

paired_user_bootstrap.method: Resample validation users with replacement, rescore both models on the same resampled users, take the difference. 2000 reps, seed 7. scripts/paired_bootstrap.py.

reference_swa7_vs_fm_root.note: Recomputed here for comparison: the incumbent's own gain over fm-root also fails 95%.

interpretation: 008 is the best validation candidate and is significantly better than the FM root under a paired user bootstrap (P=0.990, CI excludes zero), which the incumbent SWA7 is not (P=0.934, CI includes zero). Against the incumbent itself the gain is +0.000585 with P=0.888 and a CI that includes zero, so it is better on this validation set at every seed tried but not proven to generalize to a differently sampled user population.
